project_specification.overview: Post-build reports extend AutoForge with three autonomous agent types (documentation, performance profiling, security audit) that run in parallel after the QA pipeline completes. They produce professional deliverables -- API docs, user guides with screenshots, performance benchmarks with grades, and OWASP Top 10 security audits -- committed directly to the project repository. The security agent can mark features as failing to prevent shipping critical vulnerabilities. This is an internal feature addition to the existing AutoForge codebase.

prerequisites.environment_setup: - Python 3.11+ with venv - Node.js 20+ with npm - Existing AutoForge installation with all dependencies - Claude Code CLI (for running post-build agents) - Playwright MCP server (for screenshots, page timing, auth testing)

core_features.prompt_templates: - System creates documentation agent prompt template at .claude/templates/docs_prompt.template.md with phases for codebase analysis, API documentation generation, user guide with Playwright screenshots, README generation, changelog from git history, and commit instructions - System creates performance profiling agent prompt template at .claude/templates/performance_prompt.template.md with phases for page load measurement via Navigation Timing API, throttled network testing via CDP, bundle size analysis, API response time benchmarking, code anti-pattern scanning, and graded report generation (A/B/C/D/F) - System creates security audit agent prompt template at .claude/templates/security_prompt.template.md with phases for npm audit, OWASP Top 10 code scanning, Playwright-based auth bypass testing, IDOR testing, HTTP security header checks, graded report generation, and feature_mark_failing for CRITICAL vulnerabilities
core_features.cli_and_agent_types: - CLI accepts --agent-type with choices including docs, performance, and security alongside existing initializer, coding, and testing types - CLI accepts --auto-post-build flag (default true) to automatically run post-build agents after QA passes - CLI accepts --skip-docs, --skip-performance, and --skip-security flags to selectively disable individual post-build agents - CLI accepts --post-build-only flag to run post-build agents on an already-built project without re-running the build pipeline
core_features.prompt_loading: - System loads docs agent prompt via get_docs_prompt() in prompts.py with app_spec.txt content injected into the template - System loads performance agent prompt via get_performance_prompt() in prompts.py with app_spec.txt content injected into the template - System loads security agent prompt via get_security_prompt() in prompts.py with app_spec.txt content injected into the template
core_features.client_configuration: - Docs agent client provides read-only feature MCP tools (feature_get_stats, feature_get_summary) plus Playwright MCP server for screenshots plus standard built-in tools with Write access scoped to docs/ and README.md - Performance agent client provides read-only feature MCP tools (feature_get_stats, feature_get_summary) plus Playwright MCP server for page timing and CDP access plus standard built-in tools with Write access scoped to docs/performance-report.md - Security agent client provides feature MCP tools including feature_mark_failing (feature_get_stats, feature_get_summary, feature_get_by_id, feature_mark_failing) plus Playwright MCP server for auth and IDOR testing plus standard built-in tools with Write access scoped to docs/security-report.md
core_features.agent_dispatch: - Agent dispatch in agent.py routes docs agent type to the documentation prompt and client configuration - Agent dispatch in agent.py routes performance agent type to the performance prompt and client configuration - Agent dispatch in agent.py routes security agent type to the security prompt and client configuration
core_features.orchestrator_spawning: - Orchestrator spawns post-build agents in parallel after QA agent completes successfully via _check_post_build_ready() - Orchestrator spawns each enabled post-build agent as an independent subprocess via _spawn_post_build_agent() using the same pattern as _spawn_testing_agent() - Orchestrator tracks post-build state with _post_build_started flag, _post_build_completed set, and running_post_build_agents dict - Post-build agents do not count toward MAX_TOTAL_AGENTS and have their own MAX_POST_BUILD_AGENTS limit of 3
core_features.orchestrator_completion: - Orchestrator detects when all enabled post-build agents have finished via _check_post_build_complete() - Orchestrator calls _finalize_project() when all post-build agents complete, emitting a project_finalized WebSocket event with report paths and grades - YOLO mode skips post-build agents entirely since there is no QA phase to trigger them
core_features.security_rerun: - Orchestrator re-enters the build pipeline when the security agent marks features as failing, resetting QA and post-build state - Orchestrator caps security audit runs at MAX_SECURITY_AUDIT_RUNS (3) to prevent infinite security-fix-security loops - Orchestrator re-runs only the security agent (not docs or performance) after features are fixed and QA passes again - Orchestrator declares the project complete with unresolved warnings if critical issues persist after 3 security audit runs
core_features.server_settings_api: - Settings API exposes post-build configuration fields (auto_post_build, docs_enabled, performance_enabled, security_enabled) via the existing settings router and global settings model - Settings API persists post-build toggles so they survive server restarts
core_features.server_agent_api: - Agent router supports starting post-build agent types (docs, performance, security) through the existing agent control endpoints - Agent router emits post_build_status WebSocket events when post-build agents start, complete, or fail, including the grade on completion - Agent router supports --post-build-only mode that verifies all features are passing before allowing post-build agents to run
core_features.ui_types_and_websocket: - TypeScript types define PostBuildStatus event with agent type (docs/performance/security), status (running/completed/failed), and optional grade (A/B/C/D/F) - TypeScript types define ProjectFinalized event with report availability and grades - useWebSocket hook handles post_build_status and project_finalized events, updating component state
core_features.ui_settings: - SettingsModal displays an Auto Post-Build Reports toggle (default on) in a new Post-Build section - SettingsModal displays individual toggles for Documentation Agent, Performance Agent, and Security Agent (all default on) - Settings toggles map to the --skip-docs, --skip-performance, --skip-security CLI flags via the settings API
core_features.ui_pipeline_status: - Pipeline status display shows a POST-BUILD phase after QA in the build progress visualization - Post-build phase shows individual status for docs, performance, and security agents with icons (gray/clock when not started, cyan/spinner when running, green/checkmark when complete) - Post-build phase displays grade badges (A/B/C/D/F with color coding) next to completed performance and security agents
core_features.ui_agent_mascots: - AgentMissionControl displays Quill (quill pen) mascot for the docs agent in a separate Post-Build section below main build agents - AgentMissionControl displays Bolt (lightning bolt) mascot for the performance agent in the Post-Build section - AgentMissionControl displays Lock (padlock) mascot for the security agent in the Post-Build section - Post-build agent cards show thinking/working/complete states following the existing mascot animation pattern
core_features.ui_report_viewer: - App displays a Reports tab group with sub-tabs for Documentation, Performance, and Security - ReportViewer component renders markdown report files read from the project filesystem via the existing filesystem API - ReportViewer displays grade badges (A-F) with color coding (green for A/B, yellow for C, red for D/F) at the top of performance and security reports - ReportViewer renders tables as proper HTML tables with pass/fail status badges and supports collapsible sections for each report phase

tables.global_settings: Note: Extends the existing GlobalSettings model in registry.py with new fields. No new tables are created. - auto_post_build (BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT 1) -- enable post-build phase - docs_enabled (BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT 1) -- enable documentation agent - performance_enabled (BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT 1) -- enable performance agent - security_enabled (BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT 1) -- enable security agent

api_endpoints_summary.settings: - GET /api/settings (existing -- now includes post-build fields) - PUT /api/settings (existing -- now accepts post-build fields)
api_endpoints_summary.agent: - POST /api/projects/{name}/agent/start (existing -- now supports agent_type: docs|performance|security) - POST /api/projects/{name}/agent/post-build-only (new -- runs only post-build agents, verifies all features passing first)
api_endpoints_summary.reports: - GET /api/projects/{name}/reports (list available reports: docs, performance, security) - GET /api/projects/{name}/reports/{type} (read report markdown content for docs|performance|security)
api_endpoints_summary.websocket: - WS /ws/projects/{name} (existing -- now emits post_build_status and project_finalized events)

ui_layout.main_structure: Note: Extends the existing AutoForge UI layout. No new pages -- new components integrate into existing views. - Pipeline status bar gains a POST-BUILD phase indicator after QA - AgentMissionControl gains a Post-Build section with three agent cards - Main content area gains a Reports tab group alongside existing tabs - SettingsModal gains a Post-Build Reports section with toggles

design_system.color_palette: Note: Uses existing AutoForge neobrutalism design tokens from globals.css. - Post-build not started: --color-neo-pending (yellow/gray) - Post-build in progress: --color-neo-progress (cyan) - Post-build complete: --color-neo-done (green) - Grade A/B badge: green (#10B981) - Grade C badge: yellow (#F59E0B) - Grade D/F badge: red (#EF4444) - Security CRITICAL badge: red (#EF4444) with bold border
design_system.typography: Note: Uses existing Inter font family and Tailwind v4 utility classes. - Grade badges: font-bold text-lg in colored pill shape - Report section headers: font-semibold text-xl - Report tables: standard Tailwind table styling with alternating row colors

ui_ux_standards.banned_patterns: - alert(), confirm(), prompt() - Use existing Modal/Toast components - Inline styles - Use Tailwind CSS classes only - Raw timestamps in reports - Format as relative time - Ungraded reports - Every performance/security report must display a grade badge
ui_ux_standards.required_components: - Grade badge component with A-F color coding - Collapsible report section component - Post-build agent status card with mascot - Pipeline phase indicator for post-build
ui_ux_standards.page_patterns: - Post-build status is read-only (no edit view needed) - Reports are read-only rendered markdown - Settings use toggle switches (existing pattern)
ui_ux_standards.feedback_protocol: - Post-build agent start: toast notification - Post-build agent complete: toast with grade (if applicable) - Post-build all complete: celebration overlay or prominent notification - Security critical found: warning toast with link to security report
ui_ux_standards.polish_requirements: - Smooth transitions between pipeline phases - Skeleton loaders while reports are being fetched - Empty state when no reports have been generated yet - Back navigation from report detail to reports list
ui_ux_standards.accessibility_basics: - Grade badges include aria-label with full text (e.g., "Performance grade: B") - Collapsible sections use proper aria-expanded attributes - Agent status cards announce state changes to screen readers

coding_standards.architecture: - Follow existing AutoForge patterns: routers in server/routers/, services in server/services/ - Follow existing UI patterns: components in ui/src/components/, hooks in ui/src/hooks/ - TypeScript interfaces for all new data types in ui/src/lib/types.ts - Python type hints on all new functions - New Python code must pass ruff check and mypy - New TypeScript code must pass npm run lint and npm run build
coding_standards.routing: - No new pages -- integrate into existing views - Reports API follows existing REST patterns in server/routers/
coding_standards.error_handling: - Post-build agent failures do not block project completion (except security CRITICAL) - Failed post-build agents are logged and reported via WebSocket - Report viewer shows graceful error state if report file is not found - Retry action available for failed post-build agents

key_interactions.automatic_post_build_flow: 1. QA agent completes successfully, marking all features as passing 2. Orchestrator detects QA completion and checks post-build configuration 3. Orchestrator spawns enabled post-build agents (docs, performance, security) in parallel 4. UI updates pipeline display to show POST-BUILD phase with agent status 5. AgentMissionControl shows Quill, Bolt, Lock mascots with working state 6. Each agent generates its report and commits to git 7. WebSocket events update UI with completion status and grades 8. All agents complete -- project finalized event emitted
key_interactions.security_failure_flow: 1. Security agent discovers CRITICAL vulnerability during audit 2. Security agent marks affected feature(s) as failing via feature_mark_failing 3. Security agent commits security-report.md with findings 4. Orchestrator detects feature failures and re-enters build pipeline 5. Coding agent picks up failing feature and fixes the vulnerability 6. Feature passes through review and testing again 7. QA agent re-runs and passes 8. Orchestrator re-runs only the security agent (not docs or performance) 9. Security agent verifies fix -- marks report as updated 10. If issues persist after 3 runs, project completes with warnings
key_interactions.manual_post_build_flow: 1. User has an already-built project with all features passing 2. User runs --post-build-only flag or clicks post-build button in UI 3. System verifies all features are passing 4. Post-build agents spawn and generate reports 5. Reports appear in the Reports tab for viewing
key_interactions.report_viewing_flow: 1. User navigates to project dashboard after post-build completes 2. User clicks Reports tab group 3. User sees sub-tabs for Documentation, Performance, Security with grade badges 4. User clicks Performance tab to view the performance report 5. Report renders with grade badge, collapsible sections, and data tables 6. User can scroll through findings and recommendations

success_criteria.functionality: - All three post-build agent types (docs, performance, security) can be spawned independently via --agent-type flag - Post-build agents spawn automatically in parallel after QA completes - Each agent produces its expected output files in the project docs/ directory - Security agent can mark features as failing for CRITICAL vulnerabilities - Security re-run logic caps at 3 audit runs without infinite loops - --post-build-only flag works on already-built projects - --skip-docs/performance/security flags correctly disable individual agents - Reports are committed to git automatically
success_criteria.user_experience: - Pipeline status clearly shows post-build phase with individual agent progress - Grade badges are visible and color-coded for quick assessment - Reports render cleanly with proper tables, code blocks, and collapsible sections - Settings toggles persist and correctly control agent behavior - Toast notifications inform user of post-build progress - Post-build agent mascots display in AgentMissionControl
success_criteria.technical_quality: - Python code passes ruff check and mypy - TypeScript code passes npm run lint and npm run build - No new console errors introduced - WebSocket events follow existing patterns - Post-build agents do not interfere with build agent process limits - Security re-run logic handles edge cases (no features to fix, max retries)
